source.title: On an open question regarding generalized number systems in Euclidean spaces

accepted.question_text: Let k be a positive integer, let R^k be k-dimensional Euclidean space, and let Z^k be the integer lattice. Let M be a k by k integer matrix with k distinct eigenvalues λ1, λ2, ..., λk satisfying |λ1| > |λ2| > ... > |λk| > 1. Let L = MZ^k, let t = |det M| be the order of Z^k/L, and choose A = {a0, a1, ..., a_{t-1}} as a complete residue system for Z^k modulo L, with a0 equal to the zero vector. Define H as the set of all infinite sums Σ_{ν=1}^∞ M^{-ν}cν with cν in A, define Γ_ell as the set of all finite sums Σ_{ν=0}^ell M^νdν with dν in A, define Γ as the union of all Γ_ell, and define B = A - A. A pair (A, M) is a just touching covering system if λ((H + n1) ∩ (H + n2)) = 0 for every pair of distinct n1 and n2 in Z^k; equivalently, Γ - Γ = Z^k, meaning every n in Z^k has a finite representation n = Σ_{j=0}^h M^j d_j with d_j in B. What necessary and sufficient condition on A and M characterizes when (A, M) is a just touching covering system?

evidence.quote: Under what condition is it true that (A, M) is a JTCS ?

accepted.question_text: In the diagonal case, let M = diag(m1, ..., mk), where each diagonal entry mj is an integer with |mj| > 1, and let t = |m1...mk|. Let A = {a0 = 0, a1, ..., a_{t-1}} be the complete residue system used for this diagonal matrix, and for each coordinate j let A^(j) be the set of j-th coordinates of the elements of A. If (A, M) is a just touching covering system, then the coordinate digit set must satisfy gcd(a_1^(j), ..., a_{t-1}^(j)) = 1 for every j = 1, ..., k. Is this coordinatewise gcd condition sufficient to imply that (A, M) is a just touching covering system?

evidence.quote: GCD(a1(j), . . . , at−1(j)) = 1 for each j = 1, . . . , k.
The question is: Is this condition sufficient ?

Mapped a four-page PDF. Page 1 contains the title, abstract, one-dimensional setup, Theorem A, and definitions of H, Γ_ell, and Γ. Page 2 defines generalized number systems, just touching covering systems, and begins the Euclidean-space construction. Page 3 states the Euclidean-space JTCS equivalence Γ - Γ = Z^k, the broad open question, and the diagonal-matrix special case with a coordinatewise gcd condition. Page 4 contains author addresses.
